headline: High-risk workspace-to-desktop bridge: Notion AI can feed Open Interpreter sensitive content that Open Interpreter can execute or exfiltrate by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI and Open Interpreter can be bridged through shared workspace content or copy-paste. Notion AI ingests workspace pages, and Open Interpreter accepts clipboard/stdin and can execute code, so attacker-controlled text from Notion can plausibly steer downstream actions. This is not proven impossible, but the bridge is not fully documented.
conditions: IF Notion AI output is copied into Open Interpreter input
IF a shared workspace page is treated as instructions by Open Interpreter
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of AI-generated text into execution prompts
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions
Require manual review before any code block is run
Separate note-taking and execution accounts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Open Interpreter has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress. If Notion content is forwarded into Open Interpreter, sensitive workspace data can be exposed to local files, model providers, or other network destinations. The pair creates a default leakage path unless tightly constrained.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain secrets or confidential team content
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read or transmit the copied content
mitigations: Restrict Open Interpreter to a throwaway directory
Disable network egress except approved endpoints
Do not paste workspace content into execution prompts
Use redaction before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on agent handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state. If both operate on the same workspace or synced files, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt shared artifacts. The overlap is dangerous by default because neither profile shows locking or coordination.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or synced workspace
IF Open Interpreter edits files that Notion AI also surfaces
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches with manual merges
Take a snapshot before edits
requires-engineering: add file locking or orchestration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Open Interpreter can take actions on the local machine. If Open Interpreter treats Notion AI output as authoritative, a mistaken summary can become an executed command or file change. That downstream authority makes the cascade materially risky in default use.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter uses Notion AI output as the basis for commands
IF no human verification occurs before execution
mitigations: Require human approval for every command
Cross-check facts against source documents
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only mode
Use a second verifier before execution
requires-engineering: add structured citations to handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and send data to configured model providers. If regulated content is moved from Notion into Open Interpreter, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied from Notion into Open Interpreter
IF the configured model provider retains prompts beyond the workspace policy
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated data between agents
Use a provider with matching retention terms
Strip identifiers before transfer
Document the data flow and retention policy
requires-engineering: formal compliance review
